dhp334:1: If a man walk in heedlessness, Craving grows within him, like the creeper;
dhp334:3: He floats from life to life, like a monkey seeking fruit in a forest.
dhp335:1: Whosoever is overcome by this fierce Craving of attachment for the world,
dhp335:3: The sorrows of such a man increase, like the luxuriant bīraṇa grass.
dhp336:1: But whosoever overcomes this fierce Craving, difficult to overcome in this world,
dhp336:3: Sorrows roll off from him, like a drop of water from a lotus leaf.
dhp337:1: Therefore, with your kind permission, I say this to you, to all as many as are here gathered together:
dhp337:3: Dig up the root of Craving, even as he who seeks the fragrant usīra root digs up the bīraṇa grass,
dhp337:5: Lest Māra crush you again and again, as a stream crushes reeds.
dhp338:1: As a tree, though it be cut down, grows up again if its root be sound and firm,
dhp338:3: So also, if the inclination to Craving be not destroyed, this suffering springs up again and again in this world.
dhp339:1: He that is in the tow of the six and thirty powerful currents running unto pleasure,
dhp339:3: Such a man, misguided, the waves of desires inclining unto lust sweep away.
dhp340:1: The currents run in all directions; the creeper buds and shoots;
dhp340:3: When you see the creeper grown, be wise and cut the root.
dhp341:1: Flowing and unctuous are a creature’s joys;
dhp341:2: Men devote themselves to pleasure and seek after happiness;
dhp341:3: Therefore do they undergo birth and decay.
dhp342:1: Pursued by Craving, men dart hither and thither like a hunted hare;
dhp342:3: Held fast by fetters and bonds, they undergo suffering repeatedly and long.
dhp343:1: Pursued by Craving, men dart hither and thither like a hunted hare.
dhp343:3: Therefore a monk should banish Craving, desiring for himself freedom from lust.
dhp344:1: He who, free from desire, inclines to desire;
dhp344:2: He who, released from desire, runs back to desire;
dhp344:3: That man, – come, behold him; released, he runs back to bondage.
dhp345:1: That bond is not strong, say the wise, which is made of iron or of wood or of babbaja;
dhp345:3: Stronger far is the bond of passionate devotion to jewels and rings, to sons and wives.
dhp346:1: That bond is indeed strong, say the wise,
dhp346:2: Which, although loose, drags men down, and is hard to untie;
dhp346:3: By cutting this bond and retiring from the world,
dhp346:4: Men win freedom from desire and leave behind them the pleasures of sense.
dhp347:1: They that are dyed with lust follow the stream of the passions
dhp347:2: As a spider runs down the web he has spun for himself.
dhp347:3: Wise men, by cutting this bond and going forth from the world,
dhp347:4: Win freedom from desire and leave behind all suffering.
dhp348:1: Give up the things of the future, give up the things of the past,
dhp348:2: Give up the things of the present; cross to the Farther Shore;
dhp348:3: If your heart is freed from every attachment,
dhp348:4: You will no more undergo birth and old age.
dhp349:1: If a man be agitated by doubt, if strong passion sway him, if he seek only that which is pleasing,
dhp349:3: Craving will increase the more; he only strengthens the bond which holds him.
dhp350:1: But whosoever takes delight in suppressing doubt, and ever mindful, meditates on that which is not pleasing,
dhp350:3: Such a man will destroy, such a man will cleave the bond of Māra.
dhp351:1: He that has reached perfection, he that is unafraid, free from Craving, devoid of lust,
dhp351:3: He that has cut out the arrows of being, such a man has reached his last state of existence.
dhp352:1: He that is free from Craving, he that is without attachment,
dhp352:2: He that is skilled to interpret words in the old dialect,
dhp352:4: He that knows the order of the letters from first to last,
dhp352:5: Such a man has received his last body, such a man is a great sage, a great man.
dhp353:1: I have overcome all things, and know all things.
dhp353:2: In all the conditions of life I am free from taint.
dhp353:3: I have renounced all, and by the destruction of Craving have attained Emancipation.
dhp353:4: Since by myself I have attained Supernatural Knowledge, to whom can I point as my teacher?
dhp354:1: The gift of the Law surpasses all gifts, the flavor of the Law surpasses all flavors,
dhp354:3: Delight in the Law surpasses all delights, the destruction of Craving overcomes all suffering.
dhp355:1: Riches destroy the foolish; they seek not the farther shore;
dhp355:3: By his craving for riches the foolish man slays himself, as if he were slaying others.
dhp356:1: Weeds ruin a field, lust ruins mankind.
dhp356:3: Therefore alms given to those that are free from lust yield abundant fruit.
dhp357:1: Weeds ruin a field, hatred ruins mankind.
dhp357:3: Therefore alms given to those that are free from hatred yield abundant fruit.
dhp358:1: Weeds ruin a field, delusion ruins mankind.
dhp358:3: Therefore alms given to those that are free from delusion yield abundant fruit.
dhp359:1: Weeds ruin a field, inordinate desire ruins mankind.
dhp359:3: Therefore alms given to those that are free from inordinate desire yield abundant fruit.
